newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares seen steady in thin pre-Xmas trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares seen steady in thin pre-Xmas trade.

text.p: German shares were expected to trade in ever-decreasing volumes, trapped in a narrow range in the run up to the Christmas holidays, dealers said on Wednesday.
"Today's trade was very quiet and it will get even quieter towards Christmas," said one trader.

The IBIS DAX, reflecting all-day electronic dealings in the DAX index of 30 top shares, was up 7.53 points at 2,816.03 by 1519 GMT, encouraged by dollar strength and supported by a firm start on Wall Street.
The DAX index had closed bourse trade at 2,820.75 points.
Dealers said news of weaker-than-expected November German M3 money supply growth of eight percent released in the morning had also been supportive for the market.

Some commentators said the figure had raised the glimmer of a hope that the Bundesbank could shave interest rates when its council members meet for the last time in 1996 on Thursday, giving the dollar a boost against the mark.
But most analysts stuck to their view that German rates would be left unchanged.
The fact that the dollar pulled above 1.55 marks was positive for German exporting sectors, particularly chemicals.
Dealers noted that shares could experience some volatility on Friday, a so-called "triple-witching" day when certain futures contracts on the DAX and its constituent stocks expire.
"We could see some rounding of positions and volatility going into Friday with the expiry of futures," said one.
But in general, dealers saw the DAX hovering between 2,800 and 2,825 points.

Shares in Germany's third largest bank Commerzbank were the most heavily traded during the day, up over two percent or 92 pfennigs at 39.36 marks in IBIS dealings, earlier touching a new year-high of 39.65 marks in bourse trade.

The stock had also risen strongly on Tuesday on renewed banking sector merger talk, although dealers said there was no particular story boosting the stock and on Tuesday the bank said it had no comment on such rumours.

One of the day's biggest gainers were shares in pharmaceutical wholesaler Gehe, encouraged by news that the company planned to pay a 1996 dividend of one mark per share plus a special payout of 30 pfennigs per share.
Gehe shares traded up almost four percent, or 3.60 marks at 96.80 marks.
